description: Two contemporary reports describe Odienné secondary-school disruption on Tuesday 23 February and an initial Monday pupil action at Lycée 2. The KOACI body also says classes resumed two days after the Toussaint holidays, which conflicts with its February date and its Monday/Tuesday chronology. Abidjanpeople supports a Monday-lead reading but does not resolve the conflicting phrase. Do not assign a canonical start date or month ownership; likely 22 February remains a discovery lead.
required_followup: Find an independent contemporaneous report, archived copy, or other direct evidence that resolves the holiday/date contradiction before coding onset or assigning the event to February.

description: The Odienné reports describe pupil disruption, school closure and movement in the streets, but give no attendance number or clear description demonstrating at least 50 people assembled. “Great majority” and school-level enrollment/closure are not turnout. The classroom complaint is not explicitly addressed to the Ivorian government or a state policy in these reports.
required_followup: Seek evidence of an actual public assembly and its size, plus an explicit demand/addressee. Keep unknowns unknown; do not infer either field from the disruption.

description: Search-only MESRS coverage reports a February staff strike over an incentive premium, but does not establish whether any qualifying public meeting or demonstration occurred. The headline claim of 500 agents is a workforce number, not attendance. The Bouaké school-lead describes a teachers’ stoppage after security problems, not a verified public assembly.
required_followup: Read contemporary bodies or original union/ministerial records to verify any actual public gathering, attendee count, demand addressee and response. Do not code a workplace stoppage alone as a mass-mobilization event.

description: Search-only leads identify Port-Bouët clashes involving residents, police and a CIE team; February clashes between Agni and Malinké communities after a local market-relocation decision at Abongoua; and a local-government workers’ general assembly with an announced action described as “without work stoppage.” These headlines/snippets do not establish attendance, a qualifying public demand, or final inclusion/exclusion. Abongoua may be an intercommunal dispute rather than a public protest, but this is not resolved from bodies.
required_followup: Review the relevant bodies and original statements; determine whether each lead involved a public assembly of at least 50 directed to the domestic state, or should be retained as a sourced exclusion.

description: Open-web searching is not equivalent to the required systematic press archive. The 23 captured search actions and 497 ordered result headers are a bounded first pass, not exhaustive country-month coverage. Several regional leads remain search-only and no systematic access to paywalled/archive indexes was available.
required_followup: Continue language and regional-press searching, including accessible official and labor sources, and retain any archive or access limitation. Do not infer no other events from this first pass.

description: A prior January body-read article announced a possible February 22 ESEF teacher action and a possible March march. February search headers resurfaced the article, but no source confirms that the announced February action occurred. This is not a coded February event or continuation.
required_followup: Find contemporary reporting or an organizer statement confirming whether the February action occurred, its actual onset, participation and demand addressee.
